title: Italian Game
description: Develop naturally and prepare a safe king.
idea: Place a pawn in the centre, develop your knight and bishop, then castle. This quiet example gives your pieces useful squares.
plans: Develop the queenside pieces after castling.
Prepare a central pawn break when your pieces are ready.
mistakes: Moving the same piece repeatedly while others stay at home.
Starting an attack before checking your king's safety.
notes: Develop a knight and attack e5.
Support a possible future d4 push.
Support e4 and open your other bishop's diagonal.

title: Caro-Kann Defence
description: Meet 1.e4 with a solid central plan.
idea: Prepare ...d5 with ...c6. In this Advance example, develop your light-squared bishop before ...e6 closes its diagonal.
plans: Finish development and get your king safe.
Challenge White's centre with a prepared ...c5 break.
mistakes: Playing ...e6 before considering your c8 bishop.
notes: White gains space in the Advance Variation.
Develop the bishop outside the pawn chain.
Support d5 after developing the bishop.
Develop toward the kingside. Castling needs further preparation.

title: Queen's Gambit
description: Offer a wing pawn to challenge the centre.
idea: The c4 pawn challenges Black's d5 pawn. This Accepted example shows how development can help White recover the offered pawn.
plans: Develop and castle rather than rushing to recover material.
Look for an e4 central expansion when it is well supported.
mistakes: Assuming Black must accept the pawn; other replies are common.
Trying to recover the pawn immediately at the cost of development.
notes: Occupy the centre with your d-pawn.
Black accepts and leaves the d-file centre.
Open the bishop's path toward c4.
Recover the pawn while developing your bishop.
